name: testfoo
description: Small arithmetic helpers for testing Foo publication and installation.
readme: # testfoo
`testfoo` is a small library for exercising the Foo registry end to end.
It intentionally has no runtime dependencies.
It exposes deterministic arithmetic helpers.
The package is intended for publication testing.
The package is also intended for installation testing.
## Installation
Add the package with `foo add testfoo`.
Install the dependency graph with `foo install`.
The resolver pins the published version in `foo.lock`.
The source bundle is verified before extraction.
Installed source is placed under `.foo/packages/`.
## Import
Import the package with `use testfoo as testfoo.`
The alias keeps every example explicit.
No initialization call is required.
No native library is required.
No environment variable is required.
## Version
The `version` constant reports the package version.
Its value for this release is `0.1.0`.
The constant is public.
The constant is immutable.
The constant can be inspected by documentation tools.
## Double
The `double` function accepts one integer.
The function returns an integer.
The result is the input multiplied by two.
The function does not allocate memory.
The function does not mutate external state.
Example: `testfoo.double(4)` produces `8`.
Example: `testfoo.double(0)` produces `0`.
Example: `testfoo.double(-3)` produces `-6`.
The function is deterministic.
The function is available on every platform.
## Square
The `square` function accepts one integer.
The function returns an integer.
The result is the input multiplied by itself.
The function does not allocate memory.
The function does not mutate external state.
Example: `testfoo.square(4)` produces `16`.
Example: `testfoo.square(0)` produces `0`.
Example: `testfoo.square(-3)` produces `9`.
The function is deterministic.
The function is available on every platform.
## Increment
The `increment` function accepts one integer.
The function returns an integer.
The result is one greater than the input.
The function does not allocate memory.
The function does not mutate external state.
Example: `testfoo.increment(4)` produces `5`.
Example: `testfoo.increment(0)` produces `1`.
Example: `testfoo.increment(-3)` produces `-2`.
The function is deterministic.
The function is available on every platform.
## Decrement
The `decrement` function accepts one integer.
The function returns an integer.
The result is one less than the input.
The function does not allocate memory.
The function does not mutate external state.
Example: `testfoo.decrement(4)` produces `3`.
Example: `testfoo.decrement(0)` produces `-1`.
Example: `testfoo.decrement(-3)` produces `-4`.
The function is deterministic.
The function is available on every platform.
## Complete example
Create an application with `foo new consumer`.
Enter the application directory.
Run `foo add testfoo`.
Run `foo install`.
Open `src/main.iv`.
Add `use testfoo as testfoo.`.
Call `testfoo.double(21)` to produce `42`.
Call `testfoo.square(6)` to produce `36`.
Call `testfoo.increment(9)` to produce `10`.
Call `testfoo.decrement(9)` to produce `8`.
Run `foo check` to validate the application.
Run `foo build` to compile the application.
## Registry behavior
Publication authenticates through GitHub.
The client cannot provide an owner ID.
The server validates the GitHub token.
The server derives an opaque ownership signature.
The numeric GitHub ID is not stored in the registry.
The source is bundled without executing package code.
The source digest is recalculated by the server.
The public declarations are extracted by the compiler.
The package record is committed to the Git registry.
The discovery index is regenerated deterministically.
The package name becomes owned by the first publisher.
Future releases require the same authenticated owner.
Published versions cannot be overwritten.
Versions can be deprecated but not unpublished.
Lockfiles continue to resolve deprecated versions exactly.
## Compatibility
The package supports every Foo target.
The package uses only integer arithmetic.
The package has no operating-system-specific behavior.
The package has no network behavior.
The package has no filesystem behavior.
The package has no concurrency behavior.
The package has no unsafe native escape.
The package has no build hook.
The package has no optional dependency.
The package has no development dependency.
## Verification
Check the package with `foo check`.
Inspect declarations with `foo doc src/main.iv`.
Confirm the working tree is clean before publishing.
Confirm the repository URL is correct before publishing.
Confirm the version is unique before publishing.
Search for the package with `foo search testfoo`.
Inspect metadata with `foo info testfoo`.
Open `/package/testfoo` in the registry website.
Verify that all four functions are listed.
Verify that the ownership field is an opaque signature.
Verify that no numeric GitHub owner ID is present.
Install from a separate consumer project.
Verify that `foo.lock` contains `testfoo@0.1.0`.
Verify that the source digest matches the registry record.
Verify that repeated installation reproduces the same files.
## License
This test package uses the MIT license.
It may be followed by another test release later.
Its published `0.1.0` source remains immutable.
Its examples are intentionally small.
Its public names follow Foo naming conventions.
